## The failure-assertion rule does not apply here

This phase declares `failure_assert: not_applicable`, so the gate does NOT
require a test asserting that a failure is produced. Your subsystem reports
problems as diagnostics or emits documents, so there is no `Result::Err` to
assert on. Every other test rule still applies in full.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
The standard library is the language's actual ceiling, and nobody has measured the ceiling. src/stdlib.rs exposes math, text, list, types, files, time, json/csv, network, bytes, console, random, testing and sys, and src/stdlib.rs:612 states outright 'Redblue has no regex, so this is a literal separator' - the regex crate is a dependency (src/testing/assertions.rs:130, src/testing/runner.rs:252) but is never reachable from a Redblue program. time offers now/sleep/format/unix and nothing else, so there is no date arithmetic. There is no itertools, no functools, no collections, no pathlib, no argparse, no logging, no encodings. Meanwhile 1,472 #[test] functions and 722 corpus files make every phase expensive, so choosing the next library by taste is how the wrong twelve get built.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Produce SURVEY.md: an evidence-anchored inventory of what Redblue's stdlib cannot do that Python/Rust/JS can, each gap cited to the file and line that proves its absence, ranked by how many realistic programs each one blocks. Rank by blocked-program count, not by how interesting the library is. Name the top ten and say which are implementable in Redblue versus which must be bindings. Implement nothing: this phase ships a document, and a phase whose output is a document must not also change code, or the ranking is never checked against anything.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-090
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] SURVEY.md exists in redblue and lists every stdlib gap with a file:line citation proving the absence, and no gap is listed without one
- [ ] the regex gap cites src/stdlib.rs:612 by line and states that the crate is a dependency used only by src/testing/
- [ ] each of the top ten gaps names at least one concrete program that cannot be written without it, written out as real Redblue source that is genuinely blocked
- [ ] each of the top ten is labelled implementable-in-Redblue or binding-required, and every binding-required entry names the Rust crate that would satisfy it
- [ ] the survey does not modify anything under src/ - `git diff --stat` shows docs only, and REPORT.md says so
- [ ] no test is deleted and `cargo test` is not run to completion as part of this phase; the phase is a document and its acceptance is reviewed by reading it
